summary.headline: Shaily FY26 revenue rose 26% to INR991 crores and PAT 83% to INR170 crores, led by Healthcare revenue up 139% to INR393 crores.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 9% YoY to INR237 crores with EBITDA margin of 29.3% and PAT of INR40 crores (up 40%). Healthcare doubled in Q4 to INR113 crores on Semaglutide pen injector commercial launches in Canada and India, while Consumer fell 31% to INR102 crores on weak US and European home furnishing demand. Management announced a semiconductor tray supply agreement and first commercial supplies to a consumer electronics customer, and an INR500 crore enabling fundraise resolution (described as annual, with no specific raise planned). The pen capacity ramp is behind plan: the 25 million-unit line added in March runs at about 45% efficiency.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR113 crores vs INR56 crores (+101%, corrected from 110% stated on call). FY26 revenue INR393 crores (+139%), 40% of consolidated revenue vs 21% in FY25.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR102 crores vs INR148 crores (-31%). FY26 revenue INR511 crores (-9%). Management cited weaker home furnishing demand in Europe and US, and some Middle East order cancellations in Q4 due to the war there.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR22 crores vs INR14 crores (+60%). FY26 revenue INR87 crores (+41%). New business confirmed in power tools and LED lighting components.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pen volume target about 36 million pens (management reconfirmed on call); FY28 target of 35-40 million pens from new capacity in supply by end FY28.
Semaglutide line target to run at 65-67 parts per minute by year end, giving a combined 40-42 million pens from the two new lines.
Management sees a 40-60 million pen range about 30 months out, based on roughly 50 million Semaglutide capacity and insulin capacity run at 60-70%.
Eye-applicator commercialisation factored into the current financial year (FY27).
Semiconductor tray supplies to start in Q4 FY27; consumer electronics plant in south India needs initial capex of about INR100 crores.
Abu Dhabi facility on plan with some buffer being used up; management expects margins to be sustained on a year-on-year basis and does not guide quarterly.
capex_capacity: 25 million pen capacity installed in March 2026 running at about 45% overall equipment efficiency (about 34-35 parts per minute on an 80 ppm line); a further 25 million capacity is due by July-August 2026 and is dedicated to Semaglutide.
Rejection rate on the line fell to 8% from about 30% previously; breakdowns at higher speed remain a work in progress.
Investment cycle from trigger to on-stream now estimated at 18-24 months, up from about 12 months.
Abu Dhabi facility to be built and scaled as planned; Middle East is purely healthcare, with hiring starting around Q1 FY27 through Sep-Oct.
Revenue potential guided by fixed asset turnover of 2-2.5x on the new fixed asset base.
Consumer electronics plant in south India: initial capex about INR100 crores; under evaluation.
demand_pricing: Pen injector order book: a INR423 crore four-year supply order from a large domestic customer was announced recently (customer not named under NDA).

Canada: two pharma customers have received approvals, both using Shaily devices; Shaily claims about 70% of top six filers in Canada. Brazil approval expected soon; Turkey and Mexico expected after Brazil.
Customers are asking for more Semaglutide product after the two Canada launches.
Semiconductor trays: supply to OSATs in India initially, with possible fab and export later; management sees it as a volume consumable business.
Consumer electronics: commercial supplies started in Q4 FY26, partly for export; management said margins will only come at scale of roughly 15-20 million units.
Pen volumes FY26 were about 23.3-23.5 million devices, below the earlier guidance of 25-26 million because capacity could not produce as projected.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new 25 million pen line be used for Semaglutide, and what is the optimal output?
qa_highlights.answer: The March 25 million line runs at about 45% efficiency; the second 25 million line due July-August is purely Semaglutide. Target is 65-67 ppm per line, giving a combined 40-42 million pens by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 pen target still 36 million or higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reconfirmed about 36 million pens for FY27 (order book frozen); the August line is the main uncertainty and a better view will come around Sep-Oct earnings call.

qa_highlights.question: What are margin and capex implications for consumer electronics?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins will be thin until scale of roughly 15-20 million units; initial plant capex about INR100 crores; no segment margin numbers given as it is B2B.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR500 crore enabling resolution signal a fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It is an annual enabling resolution for flexibility; no capital is being raised now, and any future need would be a one-off large capex for device capacity outside India and Abu Dhabi.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the semiconductor tray opportunity and how competitive is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Shaily aims to supply all Indian chip manufacturers; management called it a volume consumable business and said it expects to be sole manufacturing partner in India for this customer on technical competence in conductive plastics.

qa_highlights.question: Why did UK subsidiary margins and growth weaken?
qa_highlights.answer: Longer-term, milestone-based projects delay revenue recognition; management asked investors to view UK and UAE margins combined and to judge margins on a year-on-year basis.

risks_watch: Capacity ramp: the 25 million line at about 45% efficiency and the August line not yet installed are the main risk to the FY27 36 million pen target; supply shortfalls would be a risk to Canadian customers.
Consumer segment decline (-9% FY26, -31% Q4) with no clear recovery timeline; growth depends on US and European demand and Middle East situation.
Concentration in Semaglutide: healthcare is now 40% of revenue and revenue visibility on quarterly run rate was not provided.
Brazil, Turkey and Mexico approvals timing; Brazil expected soon but unconfirmed.
Semiconductor tray competition: Chinese, Korean and Philippine players may enter India; cost competitiveness not addressed.
Abu Dhabi facility timeline buffer being consumed; geopolitical tensions in trade corridors.
Lengthening investment cycle (18-24 months) for new lines and UK subsidiary margin pressure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on healthcare, consumer electronics and semiconductor wins, but evasive on quarterly numbers, one-off versus recurring revenue, consumer recovery timing and semiconductor competition, often citing NDA or saying it is too early. Candid that capacity is ramping slower than planned.
key_quotes: So there's only a small portion of that capacity, which is being used for Semaglutide.
The 25 million capacity that we installed in March is currently running at roughly 45% utilization, and not utilization, at operational efficiency.
I would say health care and consumer electronics represent the 2 largest opportunities.
I think we need to look at 18 to 24 months now.
